title: How to Make a Shaken Clover Club Cocktail for Spring Brunches
meta_description: Learn how to master the shaken clover club recipe for spring brunches with step‑by‑step tips, pro techniques, and the perfect Cocktail Shaker Set.
html:
When the sun is bright and the garden is in bloom, a light, frothy cocktail is the ideal brunch companion. The shaken clover club recipe delivers a blush‑pink sparkle that feels as fresh as the season itself. Below you’ll find everything you need to craft this classic drink at home—plus a quick rundown of why a quality Cocktail Shaker Set is a game‑changer for any home bartender.

What Makes a Clover Club Special?

The Clover Club originated in Philadelphia’s early‑20th‑century cocktail bars. Its signature components—gin, fresh lemon juice, raspberry syrup, and egg white—create a balanced sweet‑sour profile with a velvety foam. Because the drink is shaken, the texture is as important as the flavor. A good shaken clover club recipe hinges on three things: proper dilution, a tight seal, and vigorous shaking.

Essential Tools for a Perfect Shake

Before you pour any liquid, gather the right equipment. A sturdy, leak‑proof shaker prevents spills and keeps the foam intact. The Cocktail Shaker Set includes a Boston‑style shaker, a stainless‑steel jigger, and a fine‑mesh strainer—all designed to fit together like a puzzle. The set’s tight‑locking lid makes it easy to shake aggressively without fear of a mess, and the built‑in strainer catches ice shards for a silky finish.

Ingredients & Measurements

For a single serving, measure precisely. Over‑ or under‑dosing will throw off the balance and affect the foam.

  1. 2 oz gin (London dry or a floral gin works best)
  2. ¾ oz fresh lemon juice
  3. ½ oz raspberry syrup (simple syrup infused with fresh raspberries)
  4. ½ oz egg white (about one large egg white)
  5. Ice cubes (enough to fill the shaker halfway)

Tip: If you’re uneasy about raw egg whites, use pasteurized egg whites or a vegan foaming agent; the texture will still be luxurious.

Step‑by‑Step Shaken Clover Club Recipe

Follow these steps for a consistently smooth cocktail:

  • Dry shake. Add gin, lemon juice, raspberry syrup, and egg white to the shaker (no ice). Seal the Cocktail Shaker Set tightly and shake hard for 15 seconds. This emulsifies the egg white and creates a stable foam.
  • Wet shake. Open the shaker, add ice, re‑seal, and shake again for another 10–12 seconds. The ice chills the drink and dilutes it just enough to mellow the sharp lemon.
  • Strain. Using the set’s built‑in strainer, double‑strain the mixture into a chilled coupe glass. Double‑straining removes any ice shards and preserves the silky foam.
  • Garnish. Drop a fresh raspberry or a thin lemon twist onto the foam. The garnish adds aroma and a pop of color that makes the drink Instagram‑ready.

Serve immediately while the foam is still glossy. The result is a pink‑tinged cocktail with a light, airy head that tingles the palate.

Tips for Elevating Your Brunch Cocktail

Even a perfect recipe can be tweaked to match your brunch vibe. Here are a few ideas:

  • Herbal gin. Swap a standard London dry for a gin infused with rosemary or basil for an extra garden note.
  • Seasonal fruit. Use blackberry or strawberry syrup instead of raspberry for a different hue and flavor.
  • Bitters finish. Add a few dashes of aromatic bitters on top of the foam for complexity.
  • Batch prep. Multiply the ingredients by four, shake in a larger pitcher, and serve in individual glasses with fresh ice for larger gatherings.

Remember, the Cocktail Shaker Set’s sturdy construction makes it easy to scale up without sacrificing the shake’s vigor.

Cleaning and Storing Your Shaker Set

After the brunch crowd departs, cleaning the shaker correctly keeps it ready for the next round. Rinse the shaker, jigger, and strainer with warm water, then wash with a mild dish soap. For stubborn raspberry residue, a quick soak in a solution of one part vinegar to three parts water does the trick. Dry each piece thoroughly before storing them together in the set’s magnetic closure; this prevents scratches and keeps your tools organized.

FAQ

Can I substitute vodka for gin in the shaken clover club recipe?

Yes, vodka will work, but the botanical notes of gin are a hallmark of the original Clover Club. If you prefer a neutral spirit, expect a milder flavor profile.

Do I really need to dry shake the egg white?

Dry shaking is essential for creating a stable foam. Skipping this step can result in a thin, frothy head that collapses quickly.

Is the Cocktail Shaker Set dishwasher safe?

The stainless‑steel components are dishwasher‑safe, but hand‑washing preserves the finish longer and prevents any lingering odors.
